lines.before: Before the first push, run the strictest check once: `node .claude/first-push-check.mjs`, with the deep sweep (rule:sweep-tiers, first push). It reads every commit's whole tree (merges included) and fails on a kit path, a `never` path, or a secret-shaped file or value in ANY commit, a deleted one included; on an empty `track`, a `track` entry with no tracked file, or a wanted file that is ignored; and on a `never` file sitting unignored in the folder. It lists untracked files to decide. The owner reviews `git ls-files` against the plan. A history hit means rewriting history or a fresh repo, never "delete it in the next commit". The remote is made private first and public only after the owner checks what landed. On a pass the check records the commit; the pre-push hook lets only that commit (or its ancestors and tags) out until it is on a remote branch. **Protect main** once the repo is public and CI has a gate check: copy `.claude/kit/branch-protection.json` to `.kit/`, put the check's name in it (A26), name the act to the owner, then on their go run `gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/main/protection --input .kit/branch-protection.json` and read it back with `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/main/protection`; the rule requires that one check, blocks force pushes and deletion, needs no review for a solo owner, and lets admins bypass. Then turn on auto-merge and branch deletion (`gh api -X PATCH repos/<owner>/<repo> -F allow_auto_merge=true -F delete_branch_on_merge=true`, read back), so a PR the owner says yes to merges when its checks are green. `/methodology-kit status` flags an unprotected main. Why: the first push sets the foundation; what it carries is public for good.

lines.before: A standing grant (A27, the owner, 2026-10-31) lets named outward acts run without a yes per act. **What it holds:** `.kit/autonomy.json` names each act (for example push to main, tag, release, merge, delete a merged branch, message running sessions about a release) and the conditions it must pass. Only the owner writes or changes it; a change to it, to `.claude/autonomy.mjs` or to a gate it runs is never granted. **Before each act:** `node .claude/autonomy.mjs check <act>` reads the grant from the remote's main, never the working copy, and runs the evidence itself (tests, scrub, caps, the new test failing before the fix); a failed, missing or unreadable condition means ask the owner. **Kill switch:** the file `autonomy-off` in the Claude config folder, outside every repo; while it exists every act asks. **After:** each granted act is one line in `reports/autopilot/log.md` with its proof (the SHA or URL read back from the remote) and is reported to the owner. **Never granted:** changing the grant or its gates, deleting user data, public posts, Tier 0 rule text, or anything a test or the sweep did not pass. Projects ship with no grant (A27 `none`), so every act asks; until `autonomy.mjs` exists, no grant is in force (plan kit-autopilot). Why: the owner sets the conditions once and hears after with proof, and a gate the session can edit is no gate.
lines.after: A standing grant (A27, the owner) lets a named outward act run without a yes per act. **Two acts are granted today: auto-fix's push (rule:outward-acts) and merge, through the merge gate** (`~/.claude/kit-tools/merge-gate.mjs`, installed by `install user` outside every repo). **The grant:** allow rules the owner adds to their own Claude settings for exactly `node <config>/kit-tools/merge-gate.mjs arm *`, `disarm *` and `autofix *`; Claude never writes them. Without them, each asks. **Before arming,** each check must pass: the kill switch is absent; the PR is open, not a draft, from this repo, and the working copy is at its head; the repo allows auto-merge and deletes branches on merge; the base requires a status check; the diff touches no gate or loaded-rule path (`.github/`, `.kit/`, `.githooks/`, `.claude/`, root `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE*.md`); a sweep report for the branch names `**Covers:** <sha>` at or before the head, only `VERSION` and `CHANGELOG.md` changed after it, and the sweep audit passes it; the live PR body passes the base branch's own PR-body audit. **GO:** it runs `gh pr merge <n> --auto --squash --match-head-commit <sha>`, reads it back and logs it in `<git dir>/kit-merge-gate.log`; GitHub merges on green and deletes the branch. **NO GO:** nothing is armed, and `<git dir>/kit-merge-gate-triage.md` says what failed; the thread fixes what is its own and runs the gate again, and the rest is the owner's merge. `check <n>` runs the checks without arming. **After arming:** a push to the PR first disarms it (`disarm <n>`, logged; the pre-push hook refuses one over an armed head), then the gate runs again. A live turn tells the owner of the merge with its URL; nothing tells them of a later merge until E13 ships. **Kill switch:** `autonomy-off` in the Claude config folder: while it exists every merge and auto-fix push asks; an armed PR needs `disarm <n>`. **Never granted:** any other push, tag, release, branch deletes outside the merge, public posts, changing the grant or the gate, or anything a test or the sweep did not pass; each asks (rule:outward-acts). Why: the owner sets the conditions once and hears after with proof, and a gate the session can edit is no gate.

lines.before: The kit lives in the working folder, ready to use and continue, and never in the repo by default. The kit's own `CLAUDE.md` and the personal `CLAUDE.local.md` never go public, even when the kit is tracked; a repo that owns its `CLAUDE.md` keeps it, and the kit's goes to `CLAUDE.local.md` (the overlay). The install lists every kit path, and the owner's `never` list, in a marked block of `.git/info/exclude` (never pushed, so the names stay private) and turns on the kit's git hooks. `.kit/tracking.json`: `track` names every file the owner wants in the repo (kit files chosen to show growth are added on purpose with `git add -f`); `never` names paths that must never be committed (another party's material, private notes). Every commit runs the commit check: staging a kit file not in `track`, a `never` path or a secret-shaped file or value is blocked. Committing the whole kit (`"kit": "tracked"`) is the owner's explicit choice, for a private repo only. **Limits:** git hooks run only where the kit is installed (another computer: install there first) and are skipped by `--no-verify` - a tool that uses it is a stop-and-tell-the-owner event. Why: the kit and the owner's notes are private working material; a public repo keeps every commit forever.
